'''Eliad''' was a [[Planet/Legends|planet]] in the [[Minos Cluster/Legends|Minos Cluster]] where many wealthy noble families of the [[The galaxy/Legends|galaxy]] were exiled after the [[Rise of the Empire era|rise of the Empire]] .<ref name="GG6" />

==Description==
The climate and terrain of Eliad was extremely wide-ranging, with almost any biome being able to be found there.<ref name="GG6" /> Though few people lived on the planet compared to a core world, those few who did were exceedingly wealthy, and palaces, villas, and replica castles could be found widely across the planet.<ref name="GG6" /> The planet had little in trade aside from mineral exports; the immensely rich nobles, with absolutely nothing productive to spend their money on, instead engaged in increasingly sophisticated and demented entertainments out of sheer boredom.<ref name="GG6" /> Though separated from mainstream nobility, generations of family tradition and the highest quality education available in the galaxy made these nobles as intelligent and sophisticated as they were rich.<ref name="GG6" />

==History==
Prior to the [[Rebellion era]], the [[Battle of Eliad]] was a significant engagement of the [[Minos Cluster Campaign]] during the [[Great Galactic War]], with the planet being a noteworthy foothold strategically in the [[Minos Cluster]] as a whole.<ref name="JoMGD">[[The Journal of Master Gnost-Dural (real-life book)|''The Journal of Master Gnost-Dural'']]</ref>

Later, when [[Palpatine/Legends|Emperor Palpatine]] overthrew the [[Galactic Republic|Old Republic]] and declared his [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Empire]], he removed mass numbers of nobility from positions of power throughout the [[The galaxy/Legends|galaxy]], replacing them with Imperial representatives.<ref name="GG6" /> Instead of killing these nobles and making martyrs out of them, however, he made a bargain with them; if they agreed to permanent exile, he would allow them to keep much of their wealth and assumed status.<ref name="GG6" /> While many chose to flee or chose death rather than to submit, a large number of noble families accepted the deal, and in a mass exodus they were relocated out of the [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Empire]] and into the obscurity of the [[Outer Rim Territories/Legends|Outer Rim]].<ref name="GG6" /> In the end, three hundred thousand nobles were relocated to Eliad, along with their organic servants and massive numbers of [[Droid/Legends|droids]], where they were left to slowly and imperceptibly rot away under the weight of their own worthlessness and irrelevance - exactly as the Emeperor intended for them all along.<ref name="GG6" />

The Empire maintained a [[Lancer-class frigate/Legends|''Lancer''-Class frigate]] in orbit around the planet to watch over the nobles. Due to the Imperial unwillingness to use too much resources on a planet with a risk of rebellion so low, the frigate was mainly crewed by [[Mercenary/Legends|mercenaries]] under the watch of [[Imperial officer/Legends|Imperial officers]] and 100 [[Stormtrooper/Legends|stormtroopers]].<ref name="GG6" />
{{RPGseed}} 
During the [[Galactic Civil War/Legends|Galactic Civil War]], [[Princess/Legends|Princess]] [[Leia Organa Solo/Legends|Leia]] held many debate sessions masked as parties to encourage these deposed nobles into assisting the Rebel Alliance. After some time the nobles agreed to assist the Alliance. Together with the Princess and its escort they attacked the frigate orbiting Eliad and managed to steal it. The noble families also agreed to support the [[Alliance to Restore the Republic/Legends|Alliance]] financially.<ref name="GG6" />
{{Endgame}}
